title: A modified deep sclerectomy with or without external trabeculectomy: a comparative study

license.statement: Dove Medical Press open access licence permitting unrestricted non-commercial use (article <license>; no Creative Commons licence named); therefore private

indication: uncontrolled open-angle glaucoma (primary open-angle and pseudoexfoliation glaucoma) on maximum tolerable medical treatment, no previous eye surgery or laser trabeculoplasty, Greek Caucasian adults; 'reversed' deep sclerectomy without implant, with (group A) or without (group B) external trabeculectomy (peeling of the inner wall of Schlemm's canal); eyes with intraoperative anterior chamber perforation excluded; some patients contributed both eyes

groups.description: Group A: reversed deep sclerectomy with external trabeculectomy, 22 eyes of 18 patients (Table 3 row 'Group A'); the arm whose added technique step is under investigation
Group B: reversed deep sclerectomy alone, 20 eyes of 17 patients (Table 3 row 'Group B'); selected to match group A preoperative data by an individual unaware of the postoperative course

notes: Tonometer: Goldmann applanation tonometry preoperatively and postoperatively (Methods).
Reference: preoperative IOP under maximum tolerable medical treatment (Methods; preoperative drug counts in Table 1), recorded as preoperative_medicated.

Time units of Table 3: the second header row lists '1 day', '7 day', '1 day', '3 day', '6 day', '12 day', '18 day', '24 day', '36 day' for the nine postoperative columns (data columns C3 to C11; the header spans in the XML are misaligned and column C2 is the preoperative value). The repeated '1 day' after '7 day', the stated follow-up range of 12 to 36 months (Table 1, Abstract) and the 36-month Kaplan-Meier horizon indicate that the last seven labels are months; they are recorded as months 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24 and 36. This unit correction is an extractor interpretation flagged for review.

Role assignment: group A adds the technique step (external trabeculectomy) whose effect the study investigates, so it is recorded as treated; group B (reversed deep sclerectomy alone) is recorded as control. Both arms use the authors' modified deep sclerectomy.
Subconjunctival 5-fluorouracil injections were given for encapsulated or fibrotic blebs with raised IOP (2 eyes in group A, 4 in group B); no outcome-defined exclusion from the means is stated.
Eyes with intraoperative anterior chamber perforation were excluded from both groups (intraoperative, not postoperative, criterion).
Some patients contributed both eyes (22 eyes of 18 patients; 20 eyes of 17 patients).
